title: Magnetic Q-balls
authors: A. J. Balseyro Sebastian, Keisuke Ohashi, Muneto Nitta
abstract: We study charged soliton branches in quasi-one-dimensional chiral magnetic systems with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction, easy-axis anisotropy, and Zeeman coupling. The same static magnetic functional is equipped with two different dynamical completions: an antiferromagnetic model with second-order time derivatives and a ferromagnetic model with Berry-phase dynamics. On the helical branch selected by the static DM interaction, the problem reduces to an analytically tractable one-dimensional system for the polar angle of the order parameter. We derive the existence conditions for polar Q-balls from the curvature of the reduced effective potential and the presence of a nonzero turning point. In the antiferromagnetic case, the allowed frequency window is symmetric and can be completely closed by the combined effect of the DM coupling and the Zeeman field. At zero Zeeman field, the same reduction also supports antiferromagnetic Q-kinks, for which we obtain explicit profiles, charges, energies, and reduced-sector fission criteria. In the ferromagnetic case, the Berry phase makes the rotation frequency act as a shifted Zeeman field. As a result, north- and south-pole charged droplets are selected by opposite signs of the shifted rotation. We also show that a formal pole-to-pole solution of the ferromagnetic mechanical problem does not generally correspond to a finite-energy magnetic soliton, because the Berry term does not renormalize the physical Hamiltonian. These results clarify how charged-soliton mechanisms depend on the underlying magnetic dynamics, even when the static chiral energy is the same.
summary: This paper analyzes charged solitons in chiral magnets by comparing two dynamic models: an antiferromagnetic (AFM) and a ferromagnetic (FM) completion. It finds that while the static energy is the same, the resulting soliton mechanisms—including the selection of stable states and the existence of extended profiles—are fundamentally different due to the inclusion of the Berry phase in the FM dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and properties of charged soliton branches (Q-balls and Q-kinks) in quasi-one-dimensional chiral magnetic systems.
main_result: The nature of these charged solitons critically depends on the underlying magnetic dynamics, showing distinct behaviors when modeled by antiferromagnetic (second-order time derivatives) versus ferromagnetic (Berry-phase) completions.
method: The analysis reduces the problem to an analytically tractable one-dimensional effective potential, allowing for the derivation of existence conditions for the solitons based on potential curvature and turning points.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral magnet described by a unit vector order parameter, featuring Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction, easy-axis anisotropy, and Zeeman coupling. The dynamics are compared using two distinct completions: an AFM model and an FM model incorporating the Berry phase.
key_observables: Existence conditions for Q-balls, explicit profiles and charges for Q-kinks, and the comparison of physical energy and charge between the two dynamic models.
important_parameters: DM coupling strength (D), Zeeman field (h), and the effective coefficient $\delta = m^2 - D^2$. The comparison hinges on the sign of the rotation frequency ($\omega$) and the shifted rotation frequency ($\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the zero-longitudinal-current helical ansatz ($	ext{J}_z = 0$), and the comparison highlights that the Berry term does not renormalize the physical Hamiltonian in the FM case.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, but the text describes deriving extended profiles and comparing their energy/charge to ordinary Q-balls.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the static energy functional, then compares the resulting dynamics under AFM (second-order time derivatives) and FM (Berry phase) completions, deriving specific solutions for Q-balls and Q-kinks in each case.
why_interesting: The comparison between two different dynamical completions (AFM vs. FM) for the same static energy functional provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding how microscopic dynamics dictate macroscopic soliton stability in condensed matter systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Static helical sector for δ = 1. (a) Vacuum-subtracted effective potential around the north pole for different values of h. (b) Finite-h non-topological static profiles. As h decreases, the excursion approaches the opposite pole and the profile broadens. (c) At h = 0, the two polar vacua are degenerate and the limiting solutions are topological kink and antikink profiles.

FIG. 2: Static solutions represented as paths on the target sphere. Left: the non-topological profile leaves the north pole, reaches a turning point before the equator, and returns to the same vacuum along the same path. Right: at h = 0, the two polar vacua are degenerate and the topological kink connects the north and south poles. The antikink is the same curve with the opposite orientation.
